test_title: PYST 25: Selection Post (Matric Level) - English Language (Held On 30 June, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: english
question:
Select the idiom that gives the most appropriate meaning of the underlined phrase in the following sentence.

Our secretary is always in the mood for an argument. He must __learn to keep quiet__.
solution:
The correct answer is: **To hold his tongue**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **'learn to keep quiet'** in the sentence suggests the need for someone to learn to keep quiet or refrain from speaking, especially to avoid arguing or causing conflict.
 
• **'To hold his tongue'** is an idiom that means to refrain from speaking, to keep silent, or to avoid speaking hastily or impulsively. (चुप रहना).
 
 
• For example, "During the heated discussion, John had to remind himself to hold his tongue to avoid making the situation worse."
 
 
 
• This idiom perfectly matches the context provided as the most appropriate meaning for the underlined phrase indicating the need for the secretary to learn to maintain silence in situations where he feels inclined to argue.

Therefore, the correct answer is: ***To hold his tongue***.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **'To go through' **means to undergo or experience a difficult or challenging situation. (से गुजरना).
 
• **'To turn up'** means to arrive at a place, especially unexpectedly or without making a firm arrangement. (प्रकट होना).
 
• **'To take off'** has several meanings, including an aircraft beginning to fly, but in a more colloquial sense, it can mean to suddenly leave, or to start to succeed. (उड़ान भरना) for aircraft or (सफल होना) for success.
